newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraqi tanks dug in around Arbil.
newsitem.headline: Iraqi tanks dug in around Arbil.

text.p: Iraqi tanks were dug in on Thursday to the west and south of the northern city of Arbil, as rival Kurdish factions exchanged small arms and mortar fire.

The Iraqi forces were positioned about 15 km (nine miles) west and south of Arbil, where Iraqi forces on Saturday intervened in inter-Kurdish fighting, but took no part in the clashes, Reuters reporter Kurt Schork said after touring the area.
Iraqi forces, who now openly back the Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP) against its main rival, could not be seen in the city itself.
Near the village of Qushtapa, 22 km (14 miles) south of Arbil, KDP irregulars exchanged mortar and recoilless rifle fire with forces of the Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK)
Local residents said the PUK had opened fire first but there was no way to confirm their account.
In Washington, Central Intelligence Agency Director John Deutch said on Thursday that Iraqi tanks were pulling back from the Arbil region.
The United States launched cruise missile strikes on Tuesday and Wednesday against Iraqi military targets following Baghdad's intervention in northern Iraq.
